newsitem.title: USA: Minn. House approves $1.62 bln tax relief package.
newsitem.headline: Minn. House approves $1.62 bln tax relief package.

text.p: The Minnesota House approved a $1.62 billion tax relief package over three years that would increase the state's contribution to funding the public schools system, a fiscal analyst for the House said Monday.
Representatives approved the omnibus tax bill late Friday and the proposal must next be reconciled with a Senate tax package passed earlier in the session, fiscal analyst Matt Shands said.

The bill calls for $1.42 billion in property tax relief and $203 million in cuts in other areas over the next three years, Shands said. The bill sent to the floor had called for $1.39 billion in property tax relief and $188 million in cuts from other areas, he noted.
The bill includes a $200 million property tax rebate for renters and property owners in the current year, amounting to an 8.5 percent reduction payable in 1998, Shands said.

The state share of school funding would increase from 60 percent to 70 percent under the bill, which would be funded in part through Minnesota's projected $2.3 billion budget surplus at the end of the next biennium budget, Shands said.
The bill would impose tax caps, but makes exceptions for local governments that must deal with flood damage, debt service or state welfare reform mandates.
Gov. Arne Carlson has proposed a $1.3 billion tax relief package that would be funded through the surplus.

The Republican governor's package includes a $750 million income tax rebate, $900 million of property tax relief for commercial, industrial and multi-family property over the next three years, a $150 million education tax credit and $128 million in business and other tax reductions and higher education programs.
The next fiscal biennium for Minnesota begins on July 1.
